meta.name: Infra Readiness Hardening
meta.objective: Harden judge-gym infra for V4 launch by moving Media Cloud acquisition to the Temporal execution plane, validating full smoke/screen coverage, clearing irrelevant Convex and Railway state, and simplifying Railway bootstrap/linking so contributors can provision the stack from scratch.

knownTools: Railway MCP plus linked sincere-freedom project
Media Cloud API key in local .env.local
knownConstraints: User wants greenfield treatment: legacy code and stale state should be aggressively removed rather than migrated.
User explicitly wants Media Cloud ingestion to follow the old Firecrawl ownership model, meaning acquisition should run on the Railway/Temporal side rather than inside Convex actions.
Convex is the control plane and persistence layer; Railway/Temporal is the execution plane for long-running external I/O.
bun dev must remain agent-owned while this campaign is active.
After runtime-affecting changes to apps/engine-temporal, shared engine runtime packages, Dockerfile, or railway.toml, the worker must be redeployed and verified live before launch work resumes.
unknowns: How much of the existing Convex acquisition API should remain as public control-plane surface versus being replaced by Temporal-triggered orchestration.
Whether Media Cloud hydration should stay coupled to acquisition in the first pass or split into separate Temporal activities immediately.
What the minimal contributor bootstrap contract should be for Railway: one script, one template, or both.
notes: Current code keeps Media Cloud discovery in apps/engine-convex/convex/domain/evidence/mediacloud.ts and ingestion orchestration in evidence_service.ts and packages/evidence.ts.
Current Railway project is sincere-freedom with Temporal template services, Redis, and engine-temporal-worker already deployed.
Existing V4 paper-audit canaries are local-import based and do not require Media Cloud to run, but the user wants the acquisition architecture corrected before the broader launch campaign.

objectiveModel.terminalObjective: Harden judge-gym infra for V4 launch by moving Media Cloud acquisition to the Temporal execution plane, validating full smoke/screen coverage, clearing irrelevant Convex and Railway state, and simplifying Railway bootstrap/linking so contributors can provision the stack from scratch.
successCriteria: Media Cloud acquisition is owned by engine-temporal rather than Convex actions, with Convex used for persistence and orchestration state only.
Smoke and screen tests cover acquisition, provider routing, worker deployment, and end-to-end canary scaffolding with trustworthy validation artifacts.
Irrelevant local Convex data and unnecessary Railway services/config drift are pruned or explicitly classified as intentional.
Contributor-facing Railway bootstrap is reduced to a documented, reproducible flow that can recreate the current deployment shape from scratch.
At campaign close, the only remaining actions before V4 launch are live control-plane operations such as creating experiments, ingestion jobs, and canary runs.
nonGoals: Do not reopen the V4 paper matrix or experiment-spec campaign in this workspace.
Do not build a separate Media Cloud microservice app unless engine-temporal proves insufficient.
Do not spend time on broad lab UI work outside what is needed for infra validation.
Do not add new providers or launch new evaluation campaigns during this workspace.
dependencyPolicy: Use current repo runtime state as the implementation source of truth.
Treat the existing Railway project as the reference deployment to simplify and document, not as a permanent snowflake to preserve.
Promote only changes that improve greenfield reproducibility and reduce hidden operational coupling.

capabilityTiers.label: Infra ready
capabilityTiers.definition: Acquisition, worker deployment, smoke validation, and contributor bootstrap are coherent enough to support the V4 launch campaign.

capabilityTiers.label: Smoke verified
capabilityTiers.definition: Local and live smoke checks prove the Temporal worker, Convex control plane, and provider/external acquisition surfaces behave as expected.

capabilityTiers.label: Bootstrap simplified
capabilityTiers.definition: A new contributor can recreate the Railway-linked worker environment from repo docs and scripts with minimal manual reconstruction.

baselinePlan: Start by moving Media Cloud acquisition from Convex node actions into engine-temporal workflows/activities while preserving the existing Convex persistence model.
Use smoke-first validation: keep live checks narrow and attributable, then expand only after the execution plane is stable.
Prune stale runtime state and redundant infra only after the new path is working, so cleanup follows validation rather than preceding it.
Reduce contributor setup to a single documented Railway bootstrap path backed by repo scripts and explicit environment contracts.
progressionLadder: environment discovery -> lock current Convex/Temporal/Railway/Media Cloud execution ownership and gaps
migration planning -> compile a bounded workflow for acquisition migration and smoke validation
runtime hardening -> implement, validate, redeploy, and verify live worker behavior
cleanup and simplification -> prune irrelevant state and document/reduce contributor bootstrap

searchRegimes.focus: Use the current implementation and deployed Railway project to converge on the smallest reliable execution architecture.
Check whether any extra deployment simplifications or state-pruning opportunities materially improve contributor bootstrap.

pruneRules: Prune any branch that creates an extra standalone microservice for Media Cloud without clear scaling or ownership necessity.
Prune validation work that does not directly increase trust in the execution plane or contributor bootstrap path.
Prune legacy compatibility layers once the greenfield replacement path is validated.
escalationRules: Escalate to a deeper workflow only when the next step is a bounded implementation or cleanup slice with concrete validation.
Escalate Railway simplification only after the worker deployment contract is stable again on the migrated runtime path.
promotionRules: Promote a runtime change only if smoke coverage and live worker verification both pass.
Promote a cleanup step only if it clearly reduces stale state or contributor confusion without removing needed execution surfaces.
Promote a bootstrap contract only if it is reproducible from repo scripts/docs rather than oral history.

reviewRequired: Creating a separate acquisition microservice instead of using engine-temporal
Retaining Convex-side Media Cloud execution as the primary architecture
Expanding beyond infra hardening into V4 launch execution
stopConditions: Terminal objective met: infra is smoke-verified, cleaned, and contributor-bootstrap ready.
Hard blocker: a required external surface such as Railway or Media Cloud becomes unavailable and prevents validation.

budget.primaryCostControl: Prefer narrow live smokes and deterministic cleanup over repeated broad canary launches.
budget.executionScope: One bounded deep-workflow at a time, then direct implementation until the next strategic bottleneck.
